close_reason: Fixed in d235154: ChatTypingEvent.sender_id is now SenderId, in parity with Message and Reaction. Chat-client ws.rs test updated; new typing_event_self_sentinel_routes_to_owner covers the echo-suppression path. Parallel defect on ChatMessageEntry tracked at bd:JMAP-ly0n.22.
description:
Trigger: a downstream consumer treats ChatTypingEvent.sender_id the same way as Message.sender_id or Reaction.sender_id.

Bad behavior: crate-jmap-chat-types/src/ephemeral.rs:50 declares ChatTypingEvent.sender_id: String, but Message and Reaction use SenderId — the typed enum that maps the wire 'self' sentinel to SenderId::Owner and any other string to SenderId::Contact(s). A consumer who handles 'is the typing notification from the account owner?' has to special-case the string compare here in addition to the SenderId match elsewhere. Two compose-y bugs:
1. If a client subscribes to its own typing events for echo-suppression, this is the exact decision point and the type does not help.
2. The collision documented separately (JMAP-ly0n.1, SenderId 'self' sentinel) becomes worse here, not better: even after the SenderId collision is fixed, the typing-event code path still uses raw strings and would diverge.

Fix: change ChatTypingEvent.sender_id to SenderId (or to whatever the fix from JMAP-ly0n.1 produces). The doc comment already hand-waves this: 'The ChatContact.id of the sender (not necessarily a JMAP Id)' — the author knew this was wrong but didn't fix it.

Same issue, lower priority, on ChatPresenceEvent.contact_id (Id) — at least that one uses Id so the type kinda matches, but the contact-id-vs-sender-id distinction is muddled across the file.
title: ChatTypingEvent.sender_id is String, not SenderId — wire shape diverges from Message/Reaction
